scope: Isolated hosted platform regressions and actual installed archives. Synthetic data and provider credentials only; the final integrated source still needs normal CI. No production Reach restart or real provider sign-in.

windows.cause: node-pty 1.1.0 natural shell exit left a worker/input pipe and native console resources alive. Archive smoke completed all assertions and server.close in 4256ms but the Node process remained alive until its unchanged 30-second deadline.
fix: Pin node-pty to exact 1.1.0 for the narrow compatibility shim.
Use bundled ConPTY on Windows; release only exited PTY input socket and output worker, without killing an exited/reused PID.
Use Windows cmd and a browser shim for Claude phone sign-in; late discovery/provider responses cannot restart cancelled sign-in.

checks: Three natural PowerShell exits leave no owned console hosts while the parent remains alive.
Worker message ports close and the parent exits naturally; no process.exit shortcut or deadline increase.
Requested close and terminal liveness remain valid.
Real PTY runs a quoted .cmd provider fixture from a path containing spaces; synthetic login link/code round trip writes completion proof.
Actual npm and portable archives install; CLI/launcher, built UI/agent assets, deep links, authenticated files, traversal rejection and native terminal command/shutdown all pass.

limits: This was a scoped diagnostic, not the final combined required CI matrix.
Claude sign-in used a synthetic provider; real account authorization was not exercised.
Windows ARM and physical Windows phone/browser interactions were not exercised.
